scannerSummary.triageCaveat: Triage scores use identifier names, callback registration syntax, and direct lexical guard ordering only. Helper-sink ordering is unresolved and requires source tracing; scores prioritize review but do not prove a leak or safety.
scannerSummary.caveat: Candidates are captured writes, bounded same-file local-helper sinks, or graph-file save calls in async/registered callbacks. A save sink cue exposes target and owner selectors but does not prove ownership or a defect. Helper tracing follows identifier calls to depth 1 and reports at most 12 sinks per callback; object-method and dynamic calls may be missed. Wrappers, callers, guard control flow, and tab ownership still require manual tracing; counts and triage scores are not bug counts.

caveat: Buckets and cues prioritize manual review; file-save sink selectors are static risk cues only. Only source tracing and bounded runtime evidence establish safety or a defect.

review.ownerPath: The serialized workspace journal writer merges requested tab ids, flushes canonical owner mutations, and filters source tabs by the explicit request.
review.finalSink: Canonical journal metadata plus records for the selected workspace tabs.
review.evidence: Both callbacks only manage the single workspace-scoped writer queue; changed tab ids are unioned while a write is active, and tab payloads come from canonical workspace records rather than live DOM.

review.ownerPath: The dirty-event handler resolves the component root tab id before queueing. The queue is keyed by tab id, and the callback resolves that same tab id again before capture.
review.finalSink: checkpointCanonicalUserMutation captures and persists only when the queued owner is still the active tab; otherwise it returns before getPayload or journal writes.
review.evidence: The module-scope queue is a coalescing registry, not shared tab state: entries are keyed by owner id; completed events checkpoint synchronously at window bubble, while the timer is a propagation-stopped fallback. An inactive owner is skipped before any projection read, so this path cannot capture the sibling tab into the queued owner.
review.boundedTest: __tests__/dom/session.assignTabPayload.canonical-ui-events.test.js (14/14; includes completed-handler and stopPropagation fallback paths)

review.finalSink: Box labelPositions on the captured draw session; active module-state projection is guarded by that same owner.
review.ownerPath: executeBoxDrawPipeline binds drawSession and rejects inactive draws. The rendered SVG sits under the tab-owned workspace page; Shared.enableLabelDrag checks that page owner against the active tab. Render-cache activation rebinds label interactions with the explicit owner session.
review.evidence: The scanner captured a write inside the onDragEnd event closure, not a post-await continuation. The callback passes drawSession to commitBoxLabelStateToSession. The shared drag handler gates pointer and keyboard commits on active SVG ownership; Box cache rehydration rebinds callbacks that merge positions from owner.state.labels.
review.boundedTest: e2e/ownership/shared-svg-drag.deactivation.spec.js — Chromium 1/1: graph-title pointer drag cancels after tab switch; active Y-axis keyboard reposition updates its owner session.
